name: Evernote
tagline: Classic note-taking app with web clipper and document scanning
painPoints: Pricing restructured to paid Starter and Advanced tiers — expensive for a note app
No proactive AI; all capture and organization is manual
Frequent pricing changes and plan restructuring erode user trust
No email, calendar, or task integration for automatic knowledge capture
Performance has degraded over the years; app feels slow on mobile
metaDescription: Looking for an Evernote alternative? GAIA is source-available AI that triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across 50+ tools. Free tier included.
whyPeopleLook: Evernote was the undisputed king of note-taking for over a decade, but years of ownership changes, feature stagnation, and aggressive pricing restructuring have pushed millions of users to look elsewhere. In 2026, Evernote's paid Starter and Advanced plans — steep prices for an app that still requires you to manually clip, write, and organize everything yourself. There is no proactive AI, no email integration, and no workflow automation. Users want a tool that captures knowledge automatically from their email and meetings, not one that charges a premium for the privilege of doing it manually.
gaiaReplaces: Knowledge capture from email threads and calendar events automatically
Semantic search over your notes and correspondence
Meeting context memory without manual journaling
Task creation from notes and email without manual entry
Cross-platform note access on web, desktop, mobile, and bots
gaiaAdvantages: Knowledge is built automatically from your email and calendar: no manual clipping
Proactive surfacing means relevant notes appear when you need them
Source-available and self-hostable; Evernote is closed-source SaaS
Free tier available without aggressive pricing restructuring
Full productivity assistant beyond note storage
migrationSteps: Export your Evernote notes via File > Export as ENEX or HTML
Convert exports to Markdown and import into GAIA's memory system
Connect Gmail and Google Calendar to enrich GAIA's knowledge base automatically
Use GAIA's semantic search to retrieve knowledge instead of Evernote notebooks

faqs.question: Can GAIA replace Evernote's web clipper?
faqs.answer: GAIA does not include a browser-based web clipper. It builds knowledge automatically from your email, calendar, and connected tools. For web clipping, you can continue using a lightweight clipper tool and import saved content into GAIA's memory.

faqs.question: Is GAIA cheaper than Evernote in 2026?
faqs.answer: Evernote's Starter and Advanced plans are paid annual tiers. GAIA Pro is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month with email management, task automation, calendar integration, and 50+ tool connections. Self-hosted GAIA is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs).

faqs.question: Does GAIA have notebooks and tags like Evernote?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses graph-based memory rather than notebooks and tags. Knowledge is organized by relationships between people, projects, and events — surfaced contextually rather than browsed in a folder hierarchy.

faqs.question: Can I import my existing Evernote notes into GAIA?
faqs.answer: Yes. Export your Evernote notes as ENEX or Markdown, then import them into GAIA's memory system. GAIA will index the content for semantic search and can surface relevant notes during conversations.

comparisonRows.gaia: Knowledge platform that captures and acts: notes, email, tasks, and calendar managed by one assistant
comparisonRows.competitor: Digital note-taking and personal organization platform: capture notes, clips, scans, and documents in searchable notebooks organized by the user

comparisonRows.gaia: Capture happens automatically from email threads and calendar events, not only by typing, clipping, or scanning
comparisonRows.competitor: Manual capture: notes typed or dictated by user; web clipper for saving web pages; document scanning; audio and video transcription on paid plans

comparisonRows.gaia: AI that triages, drafts, schedules, and follows up across tools, beyond enhancing note content
comparisonRows.competitor: AI Edit and Transcribe on Starter and Advanced plans; AI features enhance note content; no autonomous monitoring, triage, or action outside the note editor

comparisonRows.gaia: Full inbox management: triage, reply drafting, and email-to-task, instead of forwarding emails into notes
comparisonRows.competitor: Email forwarding to Evernote to save email content as notes; no inbox triage, reply drafting, or email management capabilities

comparisonRows.gaia: Calendar synced and managed with meeting memory attached, so events carry their context
comparisonRows.competitor: No native calendar integration or scheduling; meeting notes can be created manually; calendar events are not synced or managed

comparisonRows.gaia: Tasks created from notes and email with priorities and deadlines, in a real hierarchy
comparisonRows.competitor: Basic task and reminder functionality inside notes; no AI-driven task creation from external sources; no dedicated project hierarchy

comparisonRows.gaia: Multi-step automations across tools described in words, replacing a passive store plus Zapier piping
comparisonRows.competitor: No native workflow automation; Zapier integration for piping external data into Evernote; primarily a passive content store

comparisonRows.gaia: Semantic search over notes plus correspondence and tasks, answering from your whole digital footprint
comparisonRows.competitor: Core strength: full-text search across typed, handwritten, and scanned content; reliable, fast search across a large note archive is a long-standing Evernote strength

comparisonRows.gaia: Source-available and self-hostable, with no acquisition-driven data concerns
comparisonRows.competitor: Closed-source SaaS; no self-hosting; data subject to Evernote's privacy policy; ownership history (Bending Spoons acquisition) has raised user data concerns

comparisonRows.gaia: Free tier without aggressive restructuring; Pro from ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month; self-hosting free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs)
comparisonRows.competitor: Free plan and paid plans available; paid hardware required.
